claims.text: multi-shop-open-requirements.md scope: the decisions already made are one shared deployment (ADR 0012), shared tables with shop_id and row-level security (ADR 0013), per-shop load limits on top of shared ones (ADR 0016), and the three-release shop_id rollout; the file does not reopen them.

ADR 0013 review condition (the sentences at the end of its consequences saying when the team must look at the decision again): the team looks again when a shop is too large for the shared tables or must be restored alone; that shop moves to its own database, the others stay in shared tables.

Two cases stay open, both in ADR 0013's review condition: a shop too large for the shared tables, and restoring one shop without taking the others back in time; CH-1 to CH-4 remain and the new scenarios are numbered from CH-5.

CH-5: the moving shop stops taking writes for at most 15 minutes (assumed), reads keep working; other shops have no refused or slower request. CH-6: done within 4 working hours (assumed); other shops lose no row and do not stop. Numbers marked 'giả định'.

Estimate: 1,000 shops, 50,000 orders a normal day; 10 large ~30% (~1,500/day each), other 990 ~35/day; largest (5,000/day) ~10%, 'đúng mức' of capacity-plan.md's trigger (>10% of busiest day, busiest = 2x normal, assumed): at, not past; doubling alone, others unchanged, passes it.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/multi-shop-open-requirements.md @ stage-4 lines 45-55; docs/design/capacity-plan.md @ stage-4 lines 16, 22, 79

claims.text: Assumptions and roles: uneven sizes (product owner, signed contracts); 15-min pause accepted (product owner with that shop); restore rare (operations team); no contract demands a separate deployment (product owner with sales); if the last is false, ADR 0012's review condition applies, out of scope.
Ranked drivers: (1) other shops see no change while one shop moves (CH-5); (2) one shop can be restored alone (CH-6); (3) a large shop's load can leave the shared tables (no CH number).
ADR 0012 review condition: a shop whose contract demands a separate system gets its own copy of the same system; the other shops are served as before.

ADR 0013: a schema or database per shop turns each release into 1,000 migration runs and each new shop into creating a schema or database, against CH-2 (a new shop needs no deploy or migration); restoring one shop means extracting its rows from a temporary restore.
PostgreSQL point-in-time recovery replays WAL for the whole server: every database on the server returns to the same moment.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3 Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery; devops.l3.point-in-time-recovery

claims.text: ADR 0016 caps each shop's load on top of the shared limits instead of moving large shops out; it is reviewed (moving the shop out) when a shop regularly needs more than its share, per ADR 0013's condition.
multi-shop-data-rollout.md adds shop_id to the shared tables over three releases.

Starting step 1 from a blank page fits only when an earlier ADR's review condition has fired or its drivers changed; listing only what is left open fits when the open cases are named in a review condition; a database for every shop fits when shops are few, so per-database migrations stay cheap.

claims.text: Choices: a contract demanding a separate deployment reopens ADR 0012, not CH-5; a 1-minute pause changes CH-5's measure first; with even shop sizes (~50/day) no shop nears the 10% trigger, driver 3 loses its reason, CH-6 stays.

claims.text: Try it: 10 largest shops at 50% of 50,000 → 2,500/day each; the other 990 → ~25/day each; conclusion holds; the shop-size assumption row changes.
CH-6's 4 working hours acts as a one-shop RTO; its 'no row lost' applies to the other shops, not the restored shop.
